ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, block A is placed on a smooth inclined plane, and 30° is marked at the bottom of the inclined plane; the light rope goes from A upward along the inclined plane, passes through the fixed pulley at the top of the inclined plane, then goes around the movable pulley on the right from which block B is suspended, and finally the other end is fixed to the ceiling at the upper right. An angle of 90° is marked between the rope segments on the two sides of the movable pulley, and B hangs below the movable pulley. Then reason: In an ideal light rope and smooth pulleys, the rope tension is the same everywhere, let it be T. For A, force balance along the direction of the inclined plane: the rope tension T upward along the inclined plane is equal to the component of gravity downward along the inclined plane, so T = mg sin30° = mg/2. Analyze the movable pulley and B as a whole: the two sides of the movable pulley each receive a rope tension T, the angle between the two forces is 90°, and the magnitude of the resultant force is 2T cos45° = √2 T, directed upward, used to balance the gravity of B. Therefore m_B g = √2 T = √2·mg/2, giving m_B = (√2/2)m.

method.method_draft: 先从图像读出：A在光滑斜面上，绳子沿斜面方向拉A，斜面倾角为30°；绳子经过左侧定滑轮后绕过右侧动滑轮，动滑轮下方挂B，动滑轮两侧绳段夹角标为90°。从题干读出：绳和滑轮均理想，A质量为m，系统静止。对A沿斜面列平衡：绳张力T等于A重力沿斜面向下分力，即T=mg sin30°=mg/2。再对动滑轮和B整体受力：两侧绳张力大小均为T，夹角90°，其合力大小为2T cos45°=sqrt(2)T，方向竖直向上以平衡B的重力。因此m_B g=sqrt(2)T=sqrt(2)mg/2，得m_B=sqrt(2)m/2。

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the inclination angle of the smooth inclined plane is $30^{\circ}$, a light rope is connected to A through two pulleys, and the other end of the light rope is fixed to the ceiling. The friction between the light rope and the pulleys is not considered. The mass of block A is m, and the masses of the pulleys are not considered. After block B is hung on, when the angle between the light ropes on the two sides of the movable pulley is $90^{\circ}$, A and B can just remain at rest. Find the mass of block B.
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, the inclination angle of the smooth inclined plane is $30^{\circ}$, a light rope is connected to A through two pulleys, and the other end of the light rope is fixed to the ceiling. The friction between the light rope and the pulleys is not considered. The mass of block A is m, and the masses of the pulleys are not considered. After block B is hung on, when the angle between the light ropes on the two sides of the movable pulley is $90^{\circ}$, A and B can just remain at rest. Find the mass of block B.
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
First describe the image: In the figure, block A is placed on a smooth inclined plane, and 30° is marked at the bottom of the inclined plane; the light rope goes from A upward along the inclined plane, passes through the fixed pulley at the top of the inclined plane, then goes around the movable pulley on the right from which block B is suspended, and finally the other end is fixed to the ceiling at the upper right. An angle of 90° is marked between the rope segments on the two sides of the movable pulley, and B hangs below the movable pulley.
Then reason: In an ideal light rope and smooth pulleys, the rope tension is the same everywhere, let it be T. For A, force balance along the direction of the inclined plane: the rope tension T upward along the inclined plane is equal to the component of gravity downward along the inclined plane, so T = mg sin30° = mg/2. Analyze the movable pulley and B as a whole: the two sides of the movable pulley each receive a rope tension T, the angle between the two forces is 90°, and the magnitude of the resultant force is 2T cos45° = √2 T, directed upward, used to balance the gravity of B. Therefore m_B g = √2 T = √2·mg/2, giving m_B = (√2/2)m.
